meta.title: lagar: Swedish law, easy to find and read
meta.description: Acts, regulations, court rulings and municipal rules from hundreds of public sources, gathered as readable text. Free, no account, open source.
hero.title: The law is public. Now you can find it too.
hero.lead: lagar gathers acts, regulations, court rulings and local rules from hundreds of public sources in one place, as text you can search and read.
hero.independent: Independent project. Not a government service.
why.title: The right to read the law
why.p1: Sweden has had the principle of public access since 1766. Official documents are open to everyone, and acts and regulations are free to read, copy and share: they are not protected by copyright.
why.p2: But public is not the same as easy to find. The rules that apply to you are published by the Riksdag, the Government, some eighty agencies, 21 county boards and 290 municipalities, each in its own way.
inside.title: What is in lagar
inside.lead: Norms are arranged in layers, from the fundamental laws down. Every layer but services is already here.
inside.fundamental_desc: The Instrument of Government and the other fundamental laws
inside.agency_desc: Regulations from work environment to food and traffic
inside.eu_desc: EU regulations and directives in Swedish, and the rulings that interpret them
inside.region_desc: County board regulations: nature reserves, hunting, fishing and traffic
inside.municipality_desc: Public order rules, fees and other local rules
sources.title: Sources
sources.lead: Texts come from official sources: Riksdag open data, court and EU publications, and the websites of agencies, county boards and municipalities. They are informational and do not replace the official publication.
sources.riksdagen_desc: the source of the SFS texts
sources.sfs_desc: the official publication of Swedish acts and ordinances
sources.lagrummet_desc: the portal of the public legal information system
sources.copyright_desc: statutes are not protected by copyright
open.title: Open source
open.p1: Every norm is a Markdown file in the repository. A collector fetches the texts from official sources, and a static JSON API makes them searchable. Everything is free under the MIT licence.
open.p2: The web app is paused while it is rebuilt, and Android and iOS apps are on the way. Meanwhile every text is in the repository on GitHub, and the API and an MCP server for AI assistants run on your own computer.
open.leis_desc: the sister project for Brazilian legislation
footer.notice: Texts in lagar are informational and do not replace Svensk författningssamling. Independent project, not affiliated with the Riksdag, the Government or any agency.
footer.credit: Made by Jackson F. de A. Mafra
catalog.series_what: Agency regulation series. Every agency that may issue regulations publishes them in its own series, such as AFS for the Swedish Work Environment Authority.
catalog.series_why: Regulations are binding rules that specify acts and ordinances within the agency's field: work environment, food, traffic, taxes and more.
catalog.shared_what: Agencies without a series of their own that publish their regulations in another agency's series.
catalog.shared_why: Their regulations are just as binding. They are collected together with the series they are published in.
catalog.counties_what: The county's regulation series. Each county administrative board publishes its regulations in a series named after the county code, such as 01FS for Stockholm County.
catalog.counties_why: Regional rules that apply in the county: nature reserves, hunting, fishing, traffic, public order and fire safety.
catalog.kommuner_what: Municipal regulation collections. Each kommun gathers its local regulations, usually on its website.
catalog.kommuner_why: Local rules that bind residents: public order regulations, waste, fees and charges, health protection.
catalog.courts_what: Guiding decisions of Swedish courts: case reports and notices published in rättspraxis.
catalog.courts_why: Precedents show how the courts apply the law and guide later cases.
catalog.sources_what: The Swedish Code of Statutes, EU law and the other legal sources lagrummet.se lists: preparatory works, registers and decisions of review boards.
catalog.sources_why: SFS holds acts and ordinances, and EU law applies directly or through Swedish law. Preparatory works and board decisions help interpret the rules but are not norms.
catalog.title: Legal sources
catalog.lead: Every source lagar tracks, with a link to the official publication and the state of collection. Each gap has an issue on GitHub.
catalog.fallback: The full list is in AGENCIES.md on GitHub.
hurdle.paths_desc: Every publisher has its own website and its own way of filing rules: a list, a register, a file archive.
hurdle.pdf_desc: Most rules from agencies, county boards and municipalities exist only as PDFs, hard to search and hard to read on a phone.
hurdle.scans_desc: Older rules are often scanned images with no text. You cannot search them, and a screen reader finds nothing.
hurdle.apis_desc: Open data exists, but often as APIs built for developers, and some sources need a key or block automated reading.
who.title: Who lagar is for
who.resident_desc: May I burn garden waste? Where may the dog run off the lead? The answer is often in a municipal regulation that is hard to find.
who.student_desc: Statutes, regulations and precedents in one place, in their current wording, linked to the official source.
who.newcomer_desc: Understanding the rules of a new country is part of settling in. It should not require knowing first how the authorities publish.
how.title: That is why lagar exists
how.lead: lagar does the work once, so nobody has to do it again.
how.collect_desc: Texts are fetched from official sources every day or week, with a link back to the original.
how.read_desc: Text is drawn out of PDF files, and scanned pages are read with OCR. OCR text is marked, and the original always prevails.
how.order_desc: Everything takes the same shape: one text file per rule, ordered by layer and issuer, searchable through an open API.
how.gaps_desc: What cannot be collected, such as sources that block automated reading, is listed openly with an issue for every gap.
